title: Startup-state matrix
description: engineering/startup_states.yaml. The highest-value artifact in this pipeline: most first-bring-up failures are floating enables, straps fought by peripherals, and back-powering, all of which are visible here and nowhere else. Hardware must default to a safe state before firmware runs, so FLOATING on a pin that enables current is a failure, not a note.

phases.description: Lifecycle phases evaluated. Fixed set by default; declared here so reports and checks agree on ordering.

criticality.description: What an unsafe state on this signal costs. 'enables_current' means an unintended assertion switches real power -- motors, heaters, RF PAs -- so an unsafe state blocks release rather than warning.

driver.description: What drives this net, and whether that driver is powered in each phase.

pull.description: External pull holding the net when nothing drives it. This is what turns FLOATING into a defined level, and its absence is the defect the matrix exists to expose.

rail.description: Which rail the pull references. A pull to a rail that is absent in an early phase does not hold the net in that phase -- a common and easily missed error.

receiver_devices.description: Devices that consume this signal, with the rail each is powered from. Used by the back-power check: a driven signal into an unpowered device can forward-bias its ESD clamp and sneak-power the part.

tolerant_when_unpowered.description: Set true only with a datasheet citation permitting voltage on the pin while the supply is absent. Defaults false because most parts forbid it.

required_state.description: The safe level per phase, from the datasheet or the system's safety argument. The check compares 'states' against this instead of guessing what safe means.

states.description: Actual level in each phase, as designed. UNKNOWN is a real answer and blocks; it is never treated as acceptable.

held_by.description: What establishes this level: 'R12 pulldown to 3V3', 'MCU push-pull', 'internal pull-up'.

safe.description: Computed by the startup-state check, not asserted by hand.

boot_strap_of.description: Refdes whose boot/configuration mode this signal selects, when applicable.

computed.description: Build output from the startup-state check.
